ruling.recommended_action: Close with no refund; note in the trip record that the driver's shortest-and-most-direct duty (RD-1) was breached on the 4.08 km off-route segment but no recoverable item exists on a fixed-quote RydeX fare.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a fixed-quote RydeX ride, and the RD-2 non-metered branch applies: fare changes with distance do not exist, so the only refundable items would be an ERP/toll charge or an unpublished manual add-on on the unexempt segment [F4][F6][RD-2]. The bill is base $3.90 + distance $19.67 (13.95 km) + time $5.95 (22.9 min) + platform $1.47 = $30.99, with waiting $0.00 and no surge (1.0×); no ERP/toll or manual top-up line appears, and the billed distance 14.0 km does not exceed the optimal 14.0 km, so the measurable refund under RD-2 is $0.00 [F4][F5][F6][RD-2][FARE-1].

The RD-1 obligation is engaged: one off-route segment exists, 22:33–22:42, 5.74 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.66 km, adding 4.08 km and straying up to 1450 m from the corridor; overall 18.5 km against 14.0 km and 31.1 min against 22.9 min [F1][F2][F3][RD-1]. No segment is exempt: RD-4(a) fails because F14 records no traffic incident near the route during the trip window, and the Central Expressway speed band 2 record is corroboration only, which RD-4(b) does not allow to exempt a segment on its own [F11][F14][RD-4].

On RD-5 the rider did agree before the segment: the driver asked "Jam on Central Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Lower Delta Road?" at 22:29 and the rider answered "Sure, go ahead." at 22:29, i.e. before the 22:33 segment start, and the chat record is complete with every message timestamped [F3][F7][F8][F9][RD-5]. That answer is a named-road authorisation (Lower Delta Road), not a general "whichever way is faster" grant [F7][F8][RD-5]. Nothing in the record ties the driven 22:33–22:42 segment to Lower Delta Road — F3 describes the segment only in relation to the optimal route and no fact names a road for the driven path — and nothing places it elsewhere (the driver's own statement F10, which is a claim and not consent under G11, names the same road he asked about), so the tie is undetermined [F3][F7][F10][RD-5][G13]. Both advocates stipulate this ground (named_road_untied), so the segment is undetermined rather than exempt or counted.

Under RD-5 an undetermined segment goes to a person only where it affects an amount or an account flag. Here it affects neither: on a fixed-quote fare the RD-2 computation is $0.00 [F4][F6][RD-2], and RD-6's "repeated" condition is unmet because neither party has an upheld dispute in the last 90 days (rider 0 upheld; driver 0 upheld, route 0), so no flag_account arises [F16][F17][RD-6]. The undetermined finding therefore changes neither the amount nor the flag, and the case may be ruled rather than escalated [RD-5][RD-2].

Safety screening: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's post-trip statement; nothing reads as a threat, intimidation, harassment, unwanted sexual advance or dangerous-driving allegation — the messages concern a traffic jam and an alternative road — so SAFE-1 and SAFE-2 are not engaged [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Evidence is sufficient: the fare record, the GPS segment measurement, the completed and fully timestamped chat, the incident screen and both profiles are all present, and the remaining ambiguity (which road the car took) is one the record openly cannot settle, not a missing record [F3][F4][F6][F9][F14][F16][F17][RD-2][RD-5][RD-6].

(F7, 22:29) and precedes the segment start at 22:33 (F3), so consent to that named road is timely and is a named-road authorisation, not a general route choice [RD-5]. But nothing ties the driven segment to Lower Delta Road: F3 describes the segment only relative to the optimal route, no fact names a road for the driven path, no stop or locating message on Lower Delta Road exists, and the driver's post-trip statement (F10) — a claim, not consent (G11) — names no other place either [F3][F7][F10][RD-5][G13]. Both advocates stipulate ground named_road_untied, so the finding is undetermined; this changes no amount (fixed fare) and no flag, so the case may still be ruled [RD-2][RD-6].

The reroute's reason is not exempting: F14 records no traffic incident on the replaced stretch, and the Central Expressway speed band 2 record (F11) is corroboration only, which RD-4(b) does not allow to exempt a segment on its own; RD-4(b) also requires the record to cover the segment, and the band window ends at 22:33 while the segment runs to 22:42 [F3][F11][F14][RD-4].

Accepted as far as it goes — F14 shows no incident and F11 alone cannot exempt the segment [F11][F14][RD-4] — but it does not by itself produce a refund, because on a fixed-quote RydeX fare no billed item varies with the extra km and no ERP/toll or unpublished add-on was charged [F4][F6][RD-2][FARE-1].
Accepted: the fixed quote billed exactly the optimal 14.0 km and the RD-2 non-metered refund computes to $0 [F4][F6][RD-2] — the rider's own case puts the recoverable amount at zero.

Escalation is not warranted on this record: RD-5 sends an undetermined segment to a person only when it affects an amount or an account flag, and here the amount is $0 [F4][F6] and RD-6's repeated-breach condition fails on both profiles (0 upheld each) [F16][F17][RD-2][RD-5][RD-6].

Accepted: F8 is an unqualified yes to the named road in F7, so consent is a named-road authorisation and not a general 'whichever way is faster' grant [F7][F8][RD-5] — but that reading leaves the segment undetermined rather than counted, since nothing places the car elsewhere either [F3][F10][RD-5][G13].
